Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 87, English)
Closing Q&A After the Ram Mantra Sadhna: Mantra Shakti, Mantra Doot, and the Discipline of Surr ender

This session is a post-sadhna Q&A/debrief held the day the nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna concluded, led primarily by senior mentors (r eferred to in the transcript as Ashish Bhaiya and Robin Bhaiya) rather than Parikshit Bhaiya dir ectly, answering the sangat's practical questions and r eceiving their experiences. Standar d number ed format is used, as this session is substantially teaching-and-Q&A rather than an individual diagnostic r oll call.

1. Housekeeping: Resuming Regular Practice Practitioners are instructed to resume their regular jaap and havan from the next day onward, continuing on whatever sankalp (vow) they were previously following before the special nine-day sadhna began.

2. Clarification on the Akhand Deepak (Eternal Lamp) A practitioner asks how long to keep the akhand deepak burning at home; it is clarified that the household akhand deepak (lit for the Navratri/Ram-tattva sadhna) is separate from ongoing personal practice, and specific guidance on when to conclude it would be given the following day .

3. Teaching: Pratyaksha Kriya and Mantra Jaap Are Combined by the Guru In response to a question about why physical kriya (movement/ritual action) and mantra jaap are combined in certain sadhnas, this teaching explains that such combinations are set by the guru according to secret (guhya) considerations tied to the specific sadhna and the particular saints assigned to work on a practitioner — not something that can always be explained in full to the practitioner .

4. Important Clarification: This Sadhna's Actual Purpose This teaching explicitly clarifies that the nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna was not designed for removing negativity; its primary purpose was to increase practitioners' mantra shakti (mantra power) and to provide mantra doot (mantra messengers). Any visions, darshan, or other experiences some practitioners had were a bonus form of grace (kripa) layered on top, not the sadhna's central aim — so practitioners who did not have visions are explicitly told not to feel demotivated, since visionary experience was never the sadhna's actual purpose.

5. Teaching: Mantra Doot Take Varying Forms In response to a question about whether mantra doot appear in a fiery form, this teaching explains that mantra doot appear in dif ferent forms for dif ferent practitioners, according to each person's individual tattva (elemental/spiritual nature), by Baba's grace.

6. Teaching: Mantra Doot Remain As Long As You Keep Practicing This teaching states that mantra doot stay with a practitioner only as long as that practitioner continues their jaap; mantra doot function according to the practitioner's ongoing mantra shakti, and if a practitioner stops japping, the mantra doot cease to actively work.

7. Teaching: How to Know If Mantra Shakti Has Incr eased This teaching explains that increases in mantra shakti and mantra doot are not always felt immediately on the day of the sadhna itself — for some, experience comes quickly; for others, the increase is "saved" and becomes apparent gradually over time, especially when facing future obstacles where the added strength then becomes evident.

8. Teaching: Prayer Power (Prarthna Shakti) Incr eases Alongside Mantra Shakti This teaching confirms that as mantra shakti grows, prayer power automatically increases as well, since prayer draws on the same underlying mantra shakti.

9. Teaching: On Mental Jaap Continuing Involuntarily (Including While Asleep) In response to a question about "Jai Siyaram" continuing to run mentally even while trying to sleep, this teaching recommends practitioners favor upanshu (whispered) or spoken jaap over prolonged silent mental jaap, since unchecked 24-hour mental jaap can build excess ener gy , causing heaviness in the head, misalignment of chakras, and distraction from daily responsibilities; practitioners are encouraged to set a defined jaap quantity for themselves rather than practicing without limit.

10. Clarification on "24-Hour Sadhna" Claims This teaching clarifies that practitioners who describe doing "24-hour sadhna" via invoking gyaan tattva are not literally sitting in jaap around the clock (since sleep alone rules that out); rather , they have invoked gyaan tattva for continuous background protection, which grants added raksha (protection) throughout the day without requiring literal nonstop chanting.

1 1. Clarification: Negativity/Pitru Influence Does Not Affect Mantra Doot In response to a direct question, this teaching confirms that negativity or ancestral (pitru) influence on a practitioner does not af fect their mantra doot.

12. Guidance: Where and How to Physically Sit for Jaap This teaching advises against performing focused jaap while lying on a bed, particularly a bed also used for sleeping by a householder (grihasthi), due to the impurity (malinta) such a shared space can carry; jaap can be done informally while doing household tasks, but formal invocation-based (aahvaan) practice should happen in a reasonably clean, respectful, seated space — since mantra doot and saints who arrive during aahvaan are owed that respect. Unmarried/non-householder practitioners may sit on a bed if needed.

13. Teaching: No Blanket Dietary Restrictions in This Sadhna This teaching clarifies that, unlike some other sadhnas, no specific dietary restrictions (e.g., timing rules around salt, cutof fs on eating) were mandated for this Ram Mantra Sadhna; the only formal requirement given was twice-daily practice (morning and evening). General guidance on onion/garlic and non-vegetarian food remains permissive but is generally discouraged due to associated impurity and time cost, framed as a personal choice rather than a strict prohibition, with the option to of fset such choices with additional committed jaap.

14. On Dussehra Mantra-Chanting Timing In response to a question about whether Dussehra-period mantra chanting can be scheduled during the day rather than at night, this teaching states that such scheduling is not up to individual preference — Baba's specific order determines the timing, since the practice is guided by the guru, not run by any one person's convenience.

15. Testimony: A Vision of Bageshwar Dham's Baba One practitioner shared a vivid nighttime experience during the sadhna in which a figure resembling the well-known Bageshwar Dham baba appeared to him, asked for a ₹20 note, and then touched his agya chakra (third eye) with a finger , producing an intense electric-like sensation through his whole body — of fered as a positive, if puzzling, experience; this teaching af firms that connections with various saints during such sadhnas are a real and normal occurrence.

16. Testimony: Deep Silence and Timelessness in Meditation A practitioner described a meditative state in which all sound and sight disappeared entirely — complete silence and an altered sense of time, where ten actual minutes felt like hours — followed by a profound sense of peace dif ficult to put into words.

17. Testimony: An Extended Vision of Pr otection and Blessing Another practitioner described an elaborate vision: being taken into the cosmos by Baba under a clear blue sky , being ritually bathed with water , receiving a red shawl and a long tilak of red sindoor , being seated on a throne resting atop the coiled body of a great multi-hooded serpent whose hoods formed a canopy overhead, and then witnessing protective flames (yellow and red, without heat) rise around the throne — which Baba explained, within the vision, represented protection ensuring no harm or negativity could reach her .

18. Teaching: This Sadhna Incr eased Mantra Shakti, Not Dimensions Dir ectly In response to a question about whether "dimensions" also rise during this sadhna, this teaching clarifies that the sadhna specifically increases mantra shakti; dimensional
advancement occurs only as an indirect consequence of ongoing mantra jaap and growing mantra ener gy , not as something this sadhna directly tar gets.

19. Teaching: Effects on Daily Practice Going Forward This teaching confirms that increased mantra shakti from this sadhna will show up as a dif ference in daily jaap going forward, though such dif ferences are typically felt gradually rather than as a sudden, singleday transformation.

20. Teaching: No Sadhna Is Ever "100% Complete" This teaching states that no single sadhna ever brings a practitioner to full completion; each sadhna raises a practitioner a certain number of steps in an ongoing journey . Mantra shakti has no fixed ceiling or absolute scale — comparing one's own level to another practitioner's is discouraged, since everyone's level and journey dif fer and cannot be meaningfully ranked against each other .

21. Extended Teaching: Humans Are Only a Medium This teaching repeatedly emphasizes that human beings — including the mentors/teachers themselves — are only a medium (madhyam) through which deities act; credit for results belongs to the devi-devatas, not the human medium, though gratitude toward the medium is also acceptable and appreciated.

22. Teaching: The Day of Wavering and the Value of Recommitment This teaching recalls that partway through the nine-day sadhna, some practitioners' resolve wavered after being asked to deepen their surrender (samarpan); those who chose not to give up, trusting they had been specifically selected by the guru for this sadhna, reportedly experienced a marked increase in positive experiences after recommitting — illustrating that a chosen sadhna's dif ficulties are themselves purposeful rather than arbitrary obstacles to escape.

23. Teaching: Don't Compar e, Stay "Empty" This teaching advises practitioners not to compare their spiritual progress or experiences to others' ("apni jagah pe koi zyada dekh raha hai") and to cultivate a mindset of remaining humble/empty (shunya) even when one has received real experiences or gifts — paradoxically framed as what allows a practitioner to keep receiving more.

24. Teaching: The Astral World Cannot Be Fully Known by Humans This teaching states that the astral world is vast beyond a human's capacity to fully comprehend, and that anyone claiming complete knowledge of it is not being truthful — only devatas can know it in full; deepening surrender is what brings a practitioner progressively more guidance, never total comprehension.

25. Teaching: Energy as a Universal "Curr ency" for Spiritual and Worldly Gr owth This teaching frames ener gy (urja) of fered to the divine as a kind of currency required for growth in the astral world, which in turn shapes growth in the physical world; a practitioner may choose to focus on worldly ef fort and be content with what comes through personal ef fort and grace, or may choose to intentionally direct ener gy toward astral growth, which then influences dimension access, connections, and deeper alignment with devashakti.

26. Teaching: Don't Stop After One Sadhna — Keep the "Hunger" Alive This teaching cautions against treating any single sadhna's fulfillment as a stopping point; after satisfaction is reached, practitioners are told to expect that fulfillment to be deliberately "emptied" again by the divine, precisely so the hunger (bhookh) for continued bhakti does not disappear — this hunger being described as essential to sustained spiritual growth.

27. Teaching: Knowledge (Gyaan) Must Accompany Power (Shakti) This teaching warns that power without discernment (vivek) can be misused, so gaining shakti through sadhna should be paired with cultivating wisdom; practitioners are cautioned against extreme emotional swings tied to visible spiritual results (excessive elation when experiences come, excessive despair when they don't), and encouraged to hold a lar ger , steadier perspective on their overall journey rather than treating any single milestone as the final goal.

28. Teaching: Keep the Larger Goal (Ishta) in View This teaching advises that intermediate spiritual gains — protection, weapons (astra), access to realms (lok), thrones (gaddi), or dimension expansion — should not become a practitioner's final craving; the intended larger goal is closeness to and attainment of one's ishta (chosen deity , e.g., Hanuman ji Maharaj or Ram), with intermediate gifts understood as steps along that path rather than endpoints in themselves.

29. Closing Guidance on Grahan Shakti (Receptive Capacity) In response to a closing question about whether a sadhna exists to specifically increase grahan shakti (one's capacity to receive/absorb spiritual ener gy), this teaching clarifies there is currently no such guru-given sadhna, because grahan shakti grows naturally and gradually with time and consistent practice rather than through a tar geted shortcut; attempting to force rapid growth (compared to trying to build a body meant to take two months of gym training in just fifteen days) risks burning out the gain and having to "pay it back" later through disruption or distraction.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna's primary purpose was increasing mantra shakti and providing mantra doot — not removing negativity and not primarily about visions; practitioners without visionary experiences should not feel demotivated. Mantra doot take varying forms per individual tattva, remain active only as long as jaap continues, and are unaf fected by negativity/pitru influence. Mantra shakti gains are often felt gradually rather than immediately , and prayer power increases alongside mantra shakti automatically . Favor upanshu/spoken jaap over unlimited silent mental jaap to avoid ener gy overload; set a defined daily jaap amount rather than practicing without limit. Avoid performing focused, invocation-based jaap while lying on a shared sleeping bed; maintain a reasonably clean, respectful, seated space out of respect for the mantra doot and saints who arrive during aahvaan. No blanket dietary restrictions were mandated for this specific sadhna; only twice-daily practice was required. No single sadhna is ever "100% complete" — mantra shakti has no fixed ceiling, and comparing one's own level to others' is discouraged since everyone's journey dif fers. Humans (including teachers/mentors) are only a medium; credit for spiritual results belongs to the devi-devatas. Power (shakti) must be paired with discernment (vivek); avoid extreme emotional swings tied to visible results, and keep the larger goal (one's ishta) in view rather than treating intermediate gifts as the final destination. Grahan shakti (receptive capacity) grows naturally with time and consistent practice; there is currently no guru-given sadhna to force it faster , and attempting to rush it risks having to "pay it back" later . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 87, English)
Closing Q&A After the Ram Mantra Sadhna: Mantra Shakti, Mantra Doot, and the Discipline of Surr ender
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn post-sadhna debrief session, led primarily by senior mentors following the conclusion of the nine-day Ram Mantra Sadhna.

Q1. When should practitioners r esume their regular jaap and havan after this special sadhna? A: Per this teaching, practitioners should resume their regular jaap and havan starting the next day , continuing on whatever sankalp (vow) they were previously following before the special nine-day sadhna began.

Q2. Was this nine-day sadhna designed to r emove negativity? A: No — per this teaching, this sadhna was not designed for removing negativity; its primary purpose was to increase practitioners' mantra shakti and to provide mantra doot (mantra messengers).

Q3. Should a practitioner feel demotivated if they did not experience visions during this sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, visions and darshan experienced by some practitioners were a bonus grace layered on top of the sadhna's actual purpose (increasing mantra shakti), not the goal itself, so not experiencing visions does not mean the sadhna failed to work.

Q4. Do mantra doot always appear in a fiery form? A: No — per this teaching, mantra doot appear in varying forms depending on each practitioner's individual tattva (spiritual nature), by Baba's grace.

Q5. Will mantra doot stay with a practitioner permanently , even if they stop practicing? A: No — per this teaching, mantra doot remain active only as long as the practitioner continues their jaap; their functioning depends on the practitioner's ongoing mantra shakti, and they stop actively working if jaap is discontinued.

Q6. How will a practitioner know if their mantra shakti has actually incr eased? A: Per this teaching, increases in mantra shakti are not always felt immediately; for some the change is noticeable right away , while for others it is "saved" and becomes apparent gradually , often surfacing clearly when facing a future obstacle.

Q7. Does incr eased mantra shakti also incr ease prayer power? A: Yes — per this teaching, prayer power increases automatically alongside mantra shakti, since both draw on the same underlying strength.

Q8. What should a practitioner do if mental jaap ("Jai Siyaram") keeps running involuntarily , even while trying to sleep? A: Per this teaching, practitioners are encouraged to favor upanshu (whispered) or spoken jaap over prolonged silent mental jaap, and to set a defined daily jaap quantity rather than practicing without limit, since unchecked continuous mental jaap can build excess ener gy and cause heaviness or distraction.

Q9. Do practitioners who describe doing "24-hour sadhna" literally sit in jaap ar ound the clock? A: No — per this teaching, such practitioners have typically invoked gyaan tattva for continuous background protection rather than literally chanting nonstop, since sleep alone makes literal 24-hour chanting impossible.
Q10. Does negativity or ancestral (pitru) influence affect a practitioner's mantra doot? A: No — per this teaching, negativity or pitru influence on a practitioner does not af fect their mantra doot.

Q1 1. Is it acceptable to do jaap while lying in bed? A: Per this teaching, formal invocation-based (aahvaan) jaap should generally not be done lying on a bed, particularly a bed also used for sleeping by a householder , due to the associated impurity; informal jaap during household tasks is fine, but focused practice should happen in a reasonably clean, seated, respectful space, since mantra doot and saints arriving during aahvaan are owed that respect.

Q12. Were there specific dietary r estrictions r equired during this Ram Mantra Sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, unlike some other sadhnas, no specific dietary restrictions were mandated for this particular sadhna; the only formal requirement was practicing twice daily , morning and evening.

Q13. Can Dussehra-period mantra chanting be scheduled during the day instead of at night, based on personal pr eference? A: No — per this teaching, such scheduling is determined by Baba's specific order , not by individual convenience, since the practice is guided by the guru rather than run according to any one person's preference.

Q14. What vision did a practitioner shar e involving a figur e resembling the Bageshwar Dham baba? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , one practitioner described a nighttime vision in which a figure resembling the well-known Bageshwar Dham baba appeared, asked for a ₹20 note, and touched his agya chakra with a finger , producing an intense electric-like sensation through his body .

Q15. Does this sadhna incr ease "dimensions," or specifically mantra shakti? A: Per this teaching, this sadhna specifically increases mantra shakti; dimensional advancement occurs only indirectly , as a downstream ef fect of ongoing mantra jaap and rising mantra ener gy , not as something this particular sadhna directly tar gets.

Q16. Will practitioners notice a differ ence in their daily jaap after completing this sadhna? A: Yes — per this teaching, increased mantra shakti will show up as a dif ference in daily jaap going forward, though this is typically felt gradually rather than as an immediate, single-day transformation.

Q17. Does any single sadhna bring a practitioner to full completion? A: No — per this teaching, no sadhna is ever "100% complete"; each sadhna raises a practitioner a certain number of steps along an ongoing journey , and mantra shakti has no fixed ceiling.

Q18. Should practitioners compar e their spiritual pr ogr ess or experiences to others in the sangat? A: No — per this teaching, comparison is explicitly discouraged, since everyone's level and journey dif fer and cannot be meaningfully measured against one another .

Q19. Who does this teaching say deserves cr edit for spiritual r esults — the human teacher/mentor or the divine? A: Per this teaching, human beings, including teachers and mentors, are described as only a medium (madhyam) through which deities act; credit for actual results belongs to the devi-devatas, though gratitude toward the human medium is also welcomed.

Q20. What happened when some practitioners' r esolve waver ed partway thr ough the nine-day sadhna? A: Per this teaching, when some practitioners were asked to deepen their surrender partway through and their resolve wavered, those who chose to trust they had been specifically selected for this sadhna and continued reportedly experienced a marked increase in positive experiences afterward.

Q21. Can the astral world ever be fully known by a human practitioner? A: No — per this teaching, the astral world is vast beyond full human comprehension, and anyone claiming complete knowledge of it is not being truthful; only devatas can know it in full, while deepening surrender brings progressively more guidance without ever reaching total comprehension.

Q22. What does this teaching mean by energy (urja) as a "curr ency" for spiritual gr owth? A: Per this teaching, ener gy of fered to the divine functions like a currency required for growth in the astral world, which in turn shapes growth in the physical world; a practitioner can choose to focus on worldly ef fort or intentionally direct ener gy toward astral growth, which influences dimension access and deeper alignment with devashakti.

Q23. Should a practitioner stop practicing once they feel satisfied after a sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, practitioners are cautioned against stopping after reaching fulfillment; the divine is described as deliberately "emptying" that fulfillment again afterward, specifically to keep the practitioner's hunger for continued bhakti alive.

Q24. Why does this teaching say power (shakti) must be pair ed with knowledge (gyaan)? A: Per this teaching, power without discernment (vivek) can be misused; practitioners are cautioned against extreme emotional swings tied to visible spiritual results and encouraged to maintain a steady , larger perspective on their overall journey .

Q25. What is described as the ultimate goal, as opposed to intermediate spiritual gifts like pr otection or dimension access? A: Per this teaching, intermediate gains such as protection, weapons, realm access, or thrones should not become a practitioner's final craving; the intended lar ger goal is closeness to and attainment of one's ishta (chosen deity), with intermediate gifts understood as steps along that path.

Q26. Is ther e a specific sadhna to incr ease grahan shakti (r eceptive capacity)? A: No — per this teaching, there is currently no guru-given sadhna specifically for this, because grahan shakti grows naturally and gradually through consistent practice over time; attempting to force rapid growth risks having to "pay it back" later through disruption or distraction, much like trying to compress two months of physical training into fifteen days.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present Q2–Q3 (this sadhna's actual purpose being mantra shakti, not negativity removal or visions) prominently and consistently , since this directly counters a likely misconception among practitioners who may compare their experience to others' visionary accounts. Present the "ener gy as currency" and "don't stop after one sadhna" teachings (Q22–Q23) as this tradition's own framework for describing sustained spiritual practice, not as universal claims. Present the Bageshwar Dham baba testimony (Q14) neutrally , as a shared personal experience within this tradition, without asserting or denying any connection to that public figure. Reinforce the "humans are only a medium" teaching (Q19) when relevant, as it reflects this tradition's explicit stance on redirecting credit toward the divine rather than toward individual teachers. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 87, Hinglish)
Ram Mantra Sadhna ke Baad ka Q&A: Mantra Shakti, Mantra Doot, aur Samarpan

Note: yeh session ek genuinely interactive post-sadhna debrief tha, jisme sangat ne bahut sar e practical questions poochhe aur apne anubhav shar e kiye. Neeche sirf woh exchanges include kiye gaye hain jo genuinely valuable clarification dete hain ya jo sabse r elatable/instructive hain.
Sangat bahan: भैया ये जो हमें जो ये मंत्र दूत िमले हैं तो ये क्या हमेशा हमारे साथ रहेंगे?

Bhaiya: हां, जब तक आप जाप करते रहेंगे तब तक। जब तक आपकी मंत्र शिक्त है तो मंत्र शिक्त के अनुसार मंत्र दूत काय� करते रहते हैं। अगर मंत्र शिक्त नहीं है, आपने जप करना छोड़ िदया, तो िफर मंत्र दूत काय� नहीं करेंगे।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek bahut practical, dir ectly-applicable clarification hai — sangat ko clearly samajh aana chahi ए ki mantra doot koi permanent gift nahi hai, balki ongoing practice se judi hui hai.
Sangat bhai: भैया सोते हुए अगर बेड पे बंदा जय िसयाराम जय िसयाराम चल रहा है तो क्या िकया जाए ? वो रुकता नहीं है कभी।

Bhaiya: देखो भाई, आप थोड़े से जागृत हुआ करो। मंत्र जाप मानिसक होता है ना तभी चलता सोते हुए या िफर चलते िफरते। अगर आप उपांशु या बोल के करते हो तो कभी ऐसे नहीं चल सकता। ज्यादा मानिसक जाप ना करें, उससे आपकी ऊज� ज्यादा बनती है, िफर आपका मन जो काम कर रहे हो उससे भटकेगा।

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek bahut common experience hai jo pr obably kaafi practitioners face karte honge, aur Bhaiya ka practical solution (upanshu/bola hua jaap pr efer karna, ek fixed limit rakhna) dir ectly actionable hai.

Sangat bhai (dr eam testimony sunate hue): भैया दो िदन पहले रात को 2:00 बजे... मुझे बागेश्वर धाम के जो बाबा हैं वह नजर आए पीले चोले में और लाल जरा पहनी हुई है। और िफर मुझे कहते हैं ₹20 का नोट दे दो। मैं पस� से िनकालता हूं और उसके बाद वो मेरे आ�ा चक्कर पे एक िफंगर से टच करते हैं और इतनी जोर से इलेिक्ट�क जैसा पूरा शरीर िहल जाता है।
Bhaiya: िबल्कुल होते हैं भाई, बहुत सारे संत कनेक्ट करते हैं आपसे , होता है िबल्कुल।
Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek striking, memorable testimony hai jise Bhaiya ne bina kisi hesitation ke ek normal, real occurr ence ke r oop mein validate kiya.
Sangat bahan (poochte hue): भैया ये साधना में हमारे डायमेंशंस भी चढ़ते हैं क्या? मतलब मंत्र दूत िमलते हैं वो समझ गया। लेिकन डायमेंशंस भी?
Bhaiya: मंत्र शिक्त बढ़ाई गई है, डायमेंशंस नहीं बढ़ाए गए आपके। ठीक है? मंत्र ऊज� जो बढ़ाई गई तो जब मंत्र जाप आप करोगे तो उससे डायमेंशन बढ़ते हैं।
Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh ek pr ecise, important distinction clarify karta hai jo shayad sangat mein confusion create kar sakta tha.
Sangat member (gratitude expr ess karte hue): भैया बहुत सारे अनुभव हुई भैया और पहले राम मंत्र साधना बहुत अच्छी हुई। आप और रॉिबन भैया और आशीष भैया को मैंने कोिट-कोिट नमन।
Bhaiya: आप धन्यवाद बाबा का ही कीिजए। मैं सबसे यह कहता हूं िक मनुष्य िसफ� माध्यम मात्र होता है। करते देवी देवता ही हैं। हमने जो कुछ भी बोला या िकया बाबा के माध्यम से ही िकया।
